title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 67-68
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 67 to 68 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'उदीर्णः सर्वतश्चक्षुरनीशः शाश्वतस्थिरः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 67 to 68 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 67 to 68.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 67 to 68** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **उदीर्णः सर्वतश्चक्षुरनीशः शाश्वतस्थिरः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**उदीर्णः सर्वतश्चक्षुरनीशः शाश्वतस्थिरः । भूशयो भूषणो भूतिर्विशोकः शोकनाशनः ॥** **अर्चिष्मानर्चितः कुम्भो विशुद्धात्मा विशोधनः । अनिरुद्धोऽप्रतिरथः प्रद्युम्नोऽमितविक्रमः ॥**

Exalted, with eyes on every side, with no lord above him is he. Eternal and steady is that God of gods. He rests on the earth, he is the ornament and the splendour, free of sorrow and the destroyer of sorrow. Bright with rays, worshipped by all, the vessel of grace is he. A wholly pure Self who purifies is that God of gods. Aniruddha, whose chariot has no rival, Pradyumna, of boundless valour.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 67 to 68 mean?
faq.a: Exalted, with eyes on every side, with no lord above him is he. Eternal and steady is that God of gods. He rests on the earth, he is the ornament and the splendour, free of sorrow and the destroyer of sorrow. Bright with rays, worshipped by all, the vessel of grace is he. A wholly pure Self who purifies is that God of gods. Aniruddha, whose chariot has no rival, Pradyumna, of boundless valour.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
